body:
- This feels like it should be split into its own note.
- We should start avoiding "out of the box". It's been painful to localize because it usually, essentially means "readily available" which, especially in the class reference, is _such a weird thing to say_. Alternatively it means "by default" so that should be said, instead.
- Very personal nitpick, saying "per-node basis" bothers me because in a perfect world we should be avoiding words that can be mistaken for concepts used by the engine (similarly to "_For instance_" -> "_For example_")
- Two sentences should be swapped around. First it should tell you that "the node inherits from its parent", then basically "this can be changed".
```suggestion
			By default, nodes inherit the physics interpolation mode from their parent. This property can enable or disable physics interpolation individually for each node, regardless of their parents' physics interpolation mode.
			[b]Note:[/b] Some node types like [VehicleWheel3D] have physics interpolation disabled by default, as they rely on their own custom solution.
```
Or similar

body:
Perhaps this means the same **exact** thing, but to me this feels more like an advice:
```suggestion
			[b]Note:[/b] When teleporting a node to a distant position, it's recommended to temporarily disable interpolation with [method Node.reset_physics_interpolation] [i]after[/i] moving the node.
```
Either that, or you'd have to explain why "you should", but that's better done in `reset_physics_interpolation`
